description: Eight sample players from the S-SMP chip of the Super Nintendo, all playing one fixed sample built into the module

params.text: Sets the playback pitch of that voice, six octaves either side of C4
Switched on, the output of the voice above is fed into this voice's phase, which is the chip's own way of cross-modulating two players
Sets the left level of that voice, -128 to 127; below zero the signal is inverted
Sets the right level of that voice, -128 to 127; below zero the signal is inverted

inputs.text: Raises the playback pitch of that voice by a volt per octave
Modulates the playback pitch of that voice, a full octave per 5V
Flips that voice's phase modulation switch while it is above 2V
Starts that voice playing on each rise past 2V and stops it when the voltage falls back to 0V
Adds to that voice's left level knob, one step per volt
Adds to that voice's right level knob, one step per volt

outputs.text: Carries the left channel of that voice
Carries the right channel of that voice

notes: nothing sounds until a gate above 2V reaches a GATE jack: the sample is a one shot, played once per rising gate
the panel is unlabelled and the maker named none of its jacks, so no tooltip appears when you hover one
there is no way to load a sample. One short recording is built into the module in the chip's compressed format and every voice plays that same recording
